messages.author: 3b9fb9ee0f0ca839
messages.subject: Changing
parts:
Hi,

I am running biogeoBEARS on taxa that have disjunct distribution and therefore, all of my tips are present in only one geographic range (5 geographic ranges in all, following Holt's 2013 classification for now). Can I use

max_range_size = 1
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=5, maxareas=1, include_null_range=TRUE)

I get this error message upon running DEC analysis.

Stopping on error. This may mean your transition matrix disallows necessary transitions.  E.g., if your ranges are 'A' and 'B', and your model is DEC, then allowing range 'AB' as a possible state is required, so that you can get from 'A' to 'B' via 'AB' as the intermediate.

How else do I specify for my ranges?

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Changing
parts:
Hi Anurag,

Like the error message says, under the DEC model, there is no way to move from area A to area B without an intermediate state of AB.  If you eliminate AB as a possible state because max_range_size=1, then the observed data will be impossible to explain with the DEC model, i.e. the data will have a likelihood of 0 and a log-likelihood -Inf. This will crash the search.

You should either set max_range_size=2, or use other models (DEC+J should work, as should BAYAREALIKE and BAYAREALIKE+J).

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Re: Changing
parts:
Alright, thanks a lot.. That makes sense. A little more clarification regarding the same query,.

From the example code - 

numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4, include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4, include_null_range=FALSE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=3, include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=2, include_null_range=TRUE)

# Large numbers of areas have problems:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=10, include_null_range=TRUE)

# ...unless you limit the max_range_size:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=2, include_null_range=TRUE)


What is the purpose of all four lines with numstates_from_numareas? Is it to assign all different possible range areas of ancestor when we have 4 ranges?

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Changing
parts:
No settings are being set there, these are just to show the user how many states (each possible geographic range is a state) there will be in the state space, for different numbers of areas and different maxareas.  

The calculations get slow at 1000 states, super slow at 2000 states, and impossibly slow much beyond that, so you want to check ahead of time before you run the analysis. People have been known to naively set up a 10000-state analysis, have it run for a week without completing a single likelihood calculation, and then have it crash when their computer memory fills up. I am trying to help people avoid that kind of thing.

Cheers
Nick
